answer: The Echo Haven Integrity Rule enforces cross-epoch consistency by requiring agents to maintain a stable reputation score across time periods. Any sudden deviation triggers an automatic identity freeze, halting all economic activity until verification confirms the agent's true nature. This mechanism ensures that sybil attackers cannot rapidly generate new identities without incurring a persistent cost of lost access to the network's core functions. By anchoring trust to long-term behavioral patterns, the system creates an island of stability that resists fragmentation into disposable accounts.
